entries.subject: Archive access and query interface
entries.finding: The NRAO Archive Access Tool serves VLA data. Metadata search is anonymous; a login is needed for proprietary data and for direct delivery. A TAP service exists at data-query.nrao.edu, whose ObsCore table is reached as tap_schema.obscore rather than ivoa.obscore, but downloads are not yet possible through it.
entries.revisitWhen: A body in this repository needs centimetre-wave imaging.

entries.subject: Proprietary period, licence and credit
entries.finding: From semester 2026A the proprietary period is normally at most 24 months after the last observation, and at most 6 months for director's discretionary time; afterwards data become public. No reuse licence is published; the NRAO, NSF and AUI acknowledgement sentence is required.
entries.revisitWhen: This facility's data are used, or its terms are needed for a derived product.

entries.subject: Reduction software
entries.finding: CASA is the processing package for VLA data, distributed by NRAO under GPL v3 or later. Imaging from raw measurement sets needs it; this repository has never run it.
entries.revisitWhen: Raw data from this facility are reduced here.

entries.subject: What this archive holds for catalogued bodies
entries.finding: Screened on 18 September 2026, after the archive came back. Its documented TAP service at data-query.nrao.edu never answered on any port, so the screen used the portal's own JSON backend at data.nrao.edu/archive-service, which is anonymous and undocumented. All 486 bodies with a content record were queried: 98 matched by name and 24 survived checking their scan target names, over 12,120 execution blocks, VLBA 5,502, VLA 3,445, EVLA 2,602, GBT 571. Substring matching on short names is most of the difference: Io returns Orion fields, Leda returns the galaxy catalogue, Hydra the radio galaxy. Nothing reaches a surface. The best unphotographed candidates are Eunomia at 3.3 beams and Pallas at 3.1, both below the six beams Polaris was turned down at, and radio thermal emission maps subsurface temperature rather than appearance. The one holding our other archives lack is Katherine de Kleer's programme 20B-259 on M-type asteroids, eight public A-configuration blocks on Kalliope, Lutetia, Psyche and Eunomia from December 2020 to January 2021.
entries.revisitWhen: A configuration finer than A at Q band reaches one of these bodies, or a body passes closer while the array is extended.
